problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, the **exact solutions** to the equation $4\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{5x}{3})+4=0,$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$  are

${x}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}=$
{{field-3}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{5x}{3})+4 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{5x}{3}) & =-4 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{5x}{3}) & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x}{3} & =-{45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{27}^{∘}+n\cdot {108}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={81}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={189}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x={297}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ 

So, the solutions to the equation, in ascending order, are 

$$
{x}_{1}={81}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={189}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}={297}^{∘}.
$$
